correctness.rationale: Multiplicative characters on F_q^* and the origin split the 2q-1 principal Fourier matrix into q-2 two-by-two blocks (scaled Gauss sums of modulus sqrt(q)) and a symmetric 3-by-3 constant block. Gram determinant ab-c²≠0 partitions every pair into perpendicular, doubly isotropic, singly isotropic or singular geometries. In the invertible groups the nontrivial-block squared singular values are respectively 1/q or φ^(±2)/q; the 3-by-3 block yields the stated exact radicals. Comparing minimum and maximum gives κ=q or φ sqrt(q), q=2 exceptional. Counting isotropic projective lines gives all optimizer multiplicities. Independently rebuilt q=3 and q=5 full principal complex Fourier matrices for every unordered projective-line pair: q=3 had 2 perpendicular and 4 singular; q=5 had 2 perpendicular, 1 doubly isotropic, 8 singly isotropic, 4 singular. Direct singular values matched q or φ sqrt(q in their proper geometries. Finite verification corroborates the all-field proof; it does not replace the character argument.
